qualification.platform: Intel Core i9-13900H, Linux 7.0.0-38-generic, KVM; processors 0 and 12
qualification.matrix: 216 encodings x 23 cases x 2 C routes x Clang/NeverC x O0/O2 on both SDKs and core classes; 1024 omitted-KVM-AC and 96 incorrect-KVM-SS cases per run separately asserted and excluded from equivalence totals
qualification.oracle: Original port bytes are intercepted and emulated by KVM. kvm_port_comparisons are NOT bare CPU equivalence; cpu_comparisons are inherited independent memory/event tests.
qualification.state: Full GPRs, usable segment caches, RFLAGS, CR2, NMI, fault frames, physical RAM and ordered device direction/port/width/value tapes; page-table A/D and unusable-cache bytes excluded from KVM equality
qualification.restart: Permission and callback failures, first/later backing stops, consumed-input page fault, IDT backing failure after input, PTE repair/IRET/retry, NMI scheduler/IRET, replaced execution context and budgets
qualification.fragment_profiles: Prepared ordinary-RAM translations with explicit atomic, page-fragment or destination-check-first input policies. Device callbacks cannot access guest RAM/state; fragment comparisons use nonaliasing page tables.

retained_counterexamples: first/native: 66+REX.W port transfer used 32 bits; corrected width precedence and added both prefix choices
second/native: KVM split INS store retains first page bytes on a later page fault; added explicit fragment profile and committed-byte reporting
probe-ac-p and final matrix: KVM omits #AC on unaligned port strings; runtime keeps #AC and its device policy, with separate discrepancy counters

probe-segment-fault-asserted-p/e: original MOV instructions retain GP for RSI and SS for RBP regardless of SS/DS prefix. Intel SDM Vol. 1 3.3.7.1 confirms ignoring legacy segment overrides. Port runtime corrected; 96 wrong-KVM-SS cases per run are asserted separately
probe-p/e: KVM can batch input reads before a fault; fault trace comparisons request one element, and no hardware/batch equivalence is inferred

specifications.title: Intel SDM, INS/OUTS and I/O permission maps
Intel SDM Vol. 1 section 3.3.7.1, ignored segment overrides and canonical faults

limitations: Explicit long-mode paged device binding only; no promotion of ordinary undefined-effect proof coverage

No physical devices, DMA, MMIO, device read-ahead, physical interrupt timing or concurrent writers; prepared-translation fragment policy is not a hardware proof for operand aliases with paging structures
KVM omits port #AC, wrongly selects #SS for SS-prefixed noncanonical OUTS, and performs batching; TSS page faults and exact bitmap-limit checks have separate architectural contract tests
Legacy i386 segmentation/task gates, complete software SMM/SGX/AEX, gather/scatter/XSAVE progress and other remaining system-state domains are still open
No final LLVM release, SDK pin or LLVM gitlink update

post_integration.change: Register DCE seed-walk reuse; merged without modifying the qualified port implementation.
